Subject: Quick intro — evaluating Redwood for GitHub integrations

Hi Ben,

I signed up for the self-serve flow yesterday and poked around the GitHub connector. Our team at OpenForge is evaluating whether to install a GitHub App vs OAuth flow — we have concerns about installation surface, webhook permissions, and whether Redwood can run in a VPC (we have strict data residency needs).

A few quick questions before a demo would be helpful so we can focus:
- Does the GitHub App require organization-wide installation or can it be repo-scoped?
- What webhook events do you need for PR/commit-level context?
- Any constraints around GitHub Enterprise Server (on-prem) compatibility?

Would love to schedule a 30-minute technical demo this week. Our engineering manager Alex Chen (alex@openforge.com) will join. We’re PST-based. Any availability Friday afternoon?

Thanks —
Priya
Head of Developer Relations, OpenForge

Hi Priya — great to meet you and thanks for signing up. I'm Ben on the SDR/AE team. Happy to run a focused 30-min session so we can answer the exact integration questions and map to your security constraints.

Quick answers up front so we can prep the demo:
- GitHub App can be repo-scoped or org-installed depending on the scope you grant; we typically recommend repo-scoped for early pilots so you can limit access.
- For PR / commit context we subscribe to push, pull_request, and pull_request_review events; we can also consume check_suite and workflow events if you want CI signals.
- We support GitHub Enterprise Server via our private deployment option (requires a VPN/bastion or an on-prem connector).

If Friday works, I have these open slots (PST):
- Fri 09/17 11:00–11:30
- Fri 09/17 14:00–14:30
- Fri 09/17 15:30–16:00

If none of those work, send a couple alternatives and we’ll accommodate. I’ve looped in Marissa (solutions engineering) to cover the technical install and on-prem questions.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
